title.en: Why are thousands protesting for education reform in India?
title.zh: 为什么数千人正在印度抗议教育改革？

summary.en: Thousands of mostly young people tried to march on India's parliament to demand changes to how the education system is run.
summary.zh: 数千名以年轻人为主的民众试图游行至印度议会，要求改变教育系统的运作方式。

body.en:
In India, tens of thousands of Gen Z protesters have taken to the streets of the capital Delhi, calling for the resignation of the country's education minister.

Starting as a satirical online movement just a couple of months ago, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is now one of India's most visible youth movements.

Despite its humorous origins, the CJP quickly became a lightning rod for disaffected young people in India, where there is high youth unemployment.

Despite its name, it's not a party. The movement is led by Abhijeet Dipke, a 30-year-old political communications strategist and former student at Boston University.

He told the BBC it started as a joke. "I thought we should all come together, maybe just start a platform."

But after offering the option to sign up to the movement through a Google form, he received tens of thousands of responses.

This propelled it forward into becoming a serious protest group, and on 9 July it announced a march to parliament to take place on 20 July. Thousands turned out in Delhi. Hundreds also attended protests and candle-lit vigils in other cities such as Mumbai, Bengaluru and Goa.

The protest took on added significance because of the treatment of Sonam Wangchuk , a well-known engineer and activist.

He went on hunger strike on 28 June in support of the CJP at Jantar Mantar, a 300-year-old observatory in central Delhi, which is often the site of protests.

On Saturday, the 59-year-old was forcibly taken to hospital , prompting outrage from CJP supporters and drawing further attention to the protest movement. He has continued fasting in hospital.

The name of the Cockroach Janta Party (the Cockroach People's Party) came about in response to comments made by India's Chief Justice, Surya Kant.

During a hearing in May, he allegedly compared unemployed young people drifting towards journalism and activism to cockroaches and parasites.

He later clarified that he had been referring specifically to people with "fake and bogus degrees", not India's youth more broadly.

The name is a parody of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power since 2014.

Spilling off the internet and into real life, young volunteers to the movement have turned up dressed as cockroaches at clean-up drives and protests.

The CJP is mostly protesting over issues they have with India's education system.

The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) is India's main entrance exam for admission to medical colleges across the country.

Nearly 2.28 million candidates sat the exam on 3 May, having studied for months - in some cases years - for the notoriously difficult paper. However, days later, it was cancelled after allegations that the questions had been leaked.

body.zh: 在印度，数万名Z世代抗议者走上首都德里街头，要求该国教育部长辞职。 几个月前，蟑螂简塔党 (CJP) 刚开始只是一场讽刺性的在线运动，如今已成为印度最引人注目的青年运动之一。 尽管起源很幽默，但 CJP 很快就成为印度青年失业率高企的心怀不满的年轻人的避雷针。 尽管有它的名字，但这并不是一个派对。该运动由 30 岁的政治传播策略师、波士顿大学前学生阿比吉特·迪普克 (Abhijeet Dipke) 领导。 他告诉英国广播公司，这最初只是一个笑话。 “我认为我们应该团结起来，也许只是创建一个平台。” 但在提供通过谷歌表格注册该运动的选项后，他收到了数以万计的回复。 这促使它成为一个严重的抗议团体，并于 7 月 9 日宣布将于 7 月 20 日向议会游行。德里有数千人参加。数百人还参加了孟买、班加罗尔和果阿等其他城市的抗议和烛光守夜活动。 由于著名工程师和活动家索南·旺楚克 (Sonam Wangchuk) 的遭遇，这次抗议活动变得更加重要。 6 月 28 日，他在简塔·曼塔天文台 (Jantar Mantar) 进行绝食抗议，以支持 CJP。简塔·曼塔天文台位于德里市中心，是一座拥有 300 年历史的天文台，这里经常发生抗议活动。 周六，这位 59 岁的人被强行送往医院，引发了 CJP 支持者的愤怒，并引起了人们对抗议运动的进一步关注。他在医院继续禁食。 蟑螂人民党（Cockroach Janta Party）的名称是为了回应印度首席大法官苏里亚·康德（Surya Kant）的评论而得名。 据称，在五月份的一次听证会上，他将转向新闻业和激进主义的失业年轻人比作蟑螂和寄生虫。 他后来澄清说，他特指的是拥有“假学位”的人，而不是更广泛的印度年轻人。 这个名字是对印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪 (Narendra Modi) 领导的印度人民党 (BJP) 的模仿，该党自 2014 年以来一直执政。 该运动的年轻志愿者从互联网上蔓延到现实生活中，他们打扮成蟑螂的样子出现在清理活动和抗议活动中。 印度人民党主要抗议印度教育体系存在的问题。 国家资格暨入学考试（NEET）是印度全国医学院入学的主要入学考试。 近 228 万名考生在 5 月 3 日参加了考试，他们为这份众所周知的难度很高的试卷学习了数月甚至数年的时间。然而，几天后，由于指控问题被泄露，该活动被取消。 这对有志之士来说是一个很大的打击，...

reflection.en: Thousands of young people in India are raising their voices, seeking a more just and equitable education system. Amos 5:24 reminds us of Yahweh's desire for justice to flow abundantly, like an unstoppable river. This longing for fairness and opportunity in education reflects a deep human need for systems that uplift and empower.
reflection.zh: 印度数千名年轻人正在发声，寻求一个更公正、更公平的教育体系。阿摩司书5:24提醒我们，雅伟渴望公义如江河般涌流，永不止息。这种对教育公平和机会的渴望，反映了人类对能够提升和赋能的制度的深层需求。

verse.textEn: Let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!
verse.textZh: 惟愿公平如大水滚滚，使公义如江河滔滔。

title.en: US launches fresh strikes on Iran, as Trump warns of retaliation for deaths of soldiers
title.zh: 美国对伊朗发动新一轮袭击，特朗普警告将对士兵死亡进行报复

summary.en: The United States has carried out new military strikes against Iran, stating the actions were intended to reduce Iran's capacity to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz. This follows a warning from former President Trump about retaliation for the deaths of American soldiers.
summary.zh: 美国对伊朗发动了新的袭击，称这些行动旨在削弱伊朗在霍尔木兹海峡袭击船只的能力。此前，前总统特朗普曾警告称，将对美国士兵的死亡进行报复。

body.en:
The US military says it launched another round of strikes against Iran to "further degrade" its capabilities to attack ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The strikes - the 10th consecutive night of attacks - come after US President Donald Trump vowed to punish Iran for the deaths of US soldiers.

In response, Iran said it struck two oil tankers in the waterway, as well as US military assets in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, state news agency IRNA reported.

President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was now fighting a "full-scale war" with the US. Trump earlier said Iran had been hit "very hard" the previous night "in honour" of three US soldiers killed recently - two in Jordan and one in Iraq.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its latest strikes had hit Iranian "military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defence systems".

Explosions were reported near the north-western city of Tabriz, where state media said one person was killed and several wounded, as well at the Gulf ports of Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini and the south-eastern ports of Chabahar and Konarak.

Centcom also insisted that commercial vessels were continuing to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran meanwhile said its forces struck two oil tankers as they attempted to transit through what it called the strait's "unsafe and hazardous southern route" and rescue teams were picking up their crews, according to state media.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz had reported being struck by an unknown projectile, forcing its crew to abandon the vessel and board a lifeboat.

It was not clear whether the tanker reported by UKMTO was among those cited by Iran.

Six fuel tankers and cargo ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to preliminary data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler. Two of these vessels had previously been sanctioned by the US for links with Iran.

This is down from eight vessels crossing on 19 July, the data shows. All but one of the crossings made on 20 July were via the northern route near Iran.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also claimed to have targeted a data centre belonging to the US company Amazon in Bahrain, according to state media on Tuesday.

The IRGC "attacked and destroyed the central data infrastructure of the American company Amazon in Bahrain with several cruise missiles," state news agency IRNA reported.

Jordan said on Tuesday that it had intercepted five drones after saying it had shot down three missiles late on Monday. Bahrain said drones launched by Iran had targeted its air navigation systems - but traffic remained unaffected. Kuwait's armed forces also said they had intercepted Iranian drones.

body.zh: 美国军方表示，对伊朗发动了新一轮打击，以“进一步削弱”其攻击霍尔木兹海峡船只的能力。 这次袭击是连续第十晚发生的袭击，此前美国总统唐纳德·特朗普发誓要因美国士兵的死亡而惩罚伊朗。 特朗普早些时候表示，伊朗前一天晚上受到了“非常严重”的打击，以“纪念”最近被杀的三名美国士兵——其中两人在约旦，一人在伊拉克。 据伊朗伊斯兰共和国通讯社报道，为应对最新一波袭击，伊朗表示袭击了水道中的两艘油轮，以及美国在巴林和科威特的军事资产。总统马苏德·佩泽什基安表示，伊朗现在正在与美国进行“全面战争”。 据官方媒体周二报道，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）表示，他们已经瞄准了位于巴林的美国亚马逊公司的基础设施。 据伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队报道，伊斯兰革命卫队“用多枚巡航导弹攻击并摧毁了位于巴林的美国亚马逊公司的中央数据基础设施”。 与此同时，德黑兰表示，尽管停火协议破裂，双方仍在通过中间人交换外交信息。 美国中央司令部（Centcom）X日表示，最新的袭击袭击了伊朗的“军事指挥中心、海上能力、导弹和无人机发射场以及防空系统”。 中央司令部表示，商船继续通过霍尔木兹海峡。 据伊朗国家通讯社伊朗通讯社报道，伊朗表示，救援队正在从试图通过重要水道的两艘油轮中转移船员。 英国海事贸易运营机构（UKMTO）表示，霍尔木兹海峡的一艘油轮据报告被不明弹丸击中，迫使船员弃船并登上救生艇。 目前尚不清楚英国海上贸易组织报告的这艘油轮是否属于伊朗引用的油轮之列。 周二晚间，国防部确认了两名美国士兵的身份——来自德克萨斯州的 19 岁伊莎贝拉·冈萨雷斯 (Pte Isabella Gonzales) 和来自夏威夷的 25 岁泰勒·詹姆斯·费汉 (Tyler James Feehan) 中尉，他们在周末伊朗对约旦穆瓦法克萨尔蒂基地的袭击中丧生。 中央司令部早些时候表示，袭击发生后，第三名军人也在行动中失踪，后来在该地区发现了身份不明的遗体。 在该地区其他地方，约旦军方周一晚间表示，在全国各地响起警报警告火力袭来之际，约旦军方击落了三枚伊朗导弹。 当天早些时候，科威特武装部队表示，他们拦截了伊朗无人机。 巴林表示，伊朗发射的无人机瞄准了其空中导航系统，但交通并未受到影响。 关于美国前一天晚上的袭击，伊朗半官方...

reflection.en: The cycle of violence, where one act leads to another, often traps nations in escalating conflict. Yahweh's word reminds us that those who live by the sword often perish by it, highlighting the tragic consequences of continuous retaliation. This sobering truth calls us to seek paths that break these destructive patterns, even when faced with provocation.
reflection.zh: 暴力循环，即一个行动导致另一个行动，常常使国家陷入不断升级的冲突之中。雅伟的话语提醒我们，凡动刀的，必死在刀下，这突显了持续报复的悲剧性后果。这个发人深省的真理呼吁我们，即使面对挑衅，也要寻求打破这些破坏性模式的道路。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Trump slaps 50% tariffs on Canada and Carney vows to 'intensify' trade talks
title.zh: 特朗普对加拿大征收50%关税，卡尼誓言“加紧”贸易谈判

summary.en: The United States has imposed 50% tariffs on Canada, marking a significant escalation in trade tensions between the two North American nations, even as officials vow to intensify trade talks.
summary.zh: 美国对加拿大征收50%的关税，标志着这两个北美邻国之间的贸易紧张关系大幅升级，尽管官员们誓言将加紧贸易谈判。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has imposed a 50% tariff on a wide range of goods imported from Canada, in retaliation for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

Everyday consumer items like wine and hockey sticks and industrial goods such as cement are among the goods targeted. However, several key exports will be spared, such as energy, potash, critical minerals and fish.

Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by saying Canada stood ready to "intensify" trade talks with the US in the coming weeks.

The White House said the duties would take effect in 30 days. It marks a major escalation in trade tensions between the North American neighbours.

These tensions have been simmering since Trump returned to office in January 2025 and unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs.

Tariffs are taxes on imported goods that are paid to the government by companies bringing in the foreign products.

The US Supreme Court ruled earlier this year that many of Trump's tariffs imposed globally under emergency powers were illegally enacted. But his latest action on Monday night uses a different, obscure law that is untested in court.

Canada, which is one of the US's closest trading partners, was one of the few countries to retaliate last year against Trump's tariffs.

It placed a 25% levy of its own on about C$30bn (£16bn; $21.7bn) worth of US goods being brought into Canada. Carney later dropped some of them.

A White House fact sheet published on Monday discussing the new tariffs said they applied regardless of whether the product was included under the existing free trade agreement between Canada, the US and Mexico, known as the USMCA.

The US has been maintaining active tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on Canadian steel, aluminium and copper. It also charges a 35% tariff on Canadian softwood lumber, alongside a 25% tax on non-US parts in cars.

Meanwhile Canada has its own 25% counter-tariff on selected imports of American steel, aluminium and vehicles.

Monday's announcement also comes in the wake of President Trump's threat to impose tariffs over Canadian wildfire smoke drifting into US cities, though this issue has not been officially mentioned as the justification for the move.

"This is the latest in a series of unilateral US trade actions that began with the US imposing a series of tariffs in direct violation of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement," Carney said in a statement on X.

Carney also cited "threats to Canadian sovereignty", possibly in reference to Trump's repeated calls to make America's northern neighbour the 51st US state.

In a post of his own on X, Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote: "If these tariffs proceed, Canada should respond tariff for tariff, dollar for dollar."

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普对从加拿大进口的多种商品征收 50% 的关税，以报复他所谓的美国汽车、乳制品和酒类的“不平等待遇”。 葡萄酒和曲棍球棒等日常消费品以及水泥等工业品都属于目标商品。然而，能源、钾肥、关键矿产和鱼类等几种主要出口产品将幸免。 加拿大总理马克·卡尼回应称，加拿大随时准备在未来几周内“加强”与美国的贸易谈判。 白宫表示，这些关税将在 30 天内生效。这标志着北美邻国之间的贸易紧张局势大幅升级。 加拿大是少数几个在 2025 年对特朗普关税进行报复的国家之一，对价值约 300 亿加元（160 亿英镑；217 亿美元）的美国商品征收 25% 的关税。卡尼后来取消了其中一些关税，但保留了对美国汽车、钢铁和铝的关税。 美国最高法院今年早些时候裁定，特朗普根据紧急权力在全球征收的许多关税都是非法实施的。但他周一晚上的最新行动使用了一项不同的、晦涩的法律，该法律未经法庭检验。 新关税适用于所有涵盖的商品，无论该产品是否包含在加拿大、美国和墨西哥之间现有的自由贸易协定（即 USMCA）内。 卡尼在 X 的一份声明中表示：“这是美国一系列单边贸易行动中的最新一起，这些行动始于美国直接违反加拿大-美国-墨西哥协议征收一系列关税。” 他还提到了“对加拿大主权的威胁”，这可能是指特朗普呼吁让美国北部邻国成为美国第 51 个州。 周一的进口税是在两国之间已经存在的贸易壁垒的基础上征收的。 美国一直对加拿大钢铁、铝和铜维持15%至50%的主动关税。华盛顿还对加拿大软木征收 35% 的关税，并对非美国汽车零部件征收 25% 的关税。 加拿大对特定进口的美国钢铁、铝和车辆征收 25% 的反关税。 周一宣布这一消息之前，特朗普总统威胁要对流入美国城市的加拿大野火烟雾征收关税。 但特朗普周一签署的行政命令中没有提及野火。 相反，这三项公告列出了加拿大此前已知的与汽车、乳制品和酒精相关的美国贸易刺激因素，这标志着两国贸易谈判的破裂。 在汽车方面，特朗普指责加拿大对美墨加协定未涵盖的美国机动车辆和零部件征税。 他认为这是“不合理的”，加拿大不向其他国家征收类似的税是对美国的歧视。 汽车...

title.en: The founder never intended it to get so big: How a 'cockroach' movement is taking hold
title.zh: 创始人从未想过它会变得如此之大：“蟑螂”运动如何扎根

summary.en: A student-led movement in India has grown into a broader campaign for accountability and restoration of trust in institutions.

body.en:
Thousands of protesters clashed with police in India on Monday as they tried to march to parliament to demand the education minister's resignation.

Police fired tear gas and charged at demonstrators with batons after they tried to breach security barricades surrounding the protest site in central New Delhi.

This marked one of the most serious confrontations in a youth-led movement's campaign against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

The protesters describe themselves as the Cockroach Janta Party, a movement that erupted online two months ago and gained momentum over alleged leaks on social media in the country’s fiercely competitive college entrance exams.

Here's how India's youth embraced an insult as a badge of resilience and turned it into a satirical political campaign that amassed millions of followers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The movement began in May after India's supreme court chief justice Surya Kant compared some unemployed young people to "cockroaches" and "parasites" during a hearing on another issue.

Abhijeet Dipke, a 30-year-old public relations graduate who was looking for work in the United States at the time, said he was "taken aback" by the comments made by Kant — who later said they were taken out of context.

Despite rapid economic growth, millions of people in the world's most populous nation struggle to find stable and well-paying jobs, fuelling discontent.

"How can the custodian of the constitution compare the youth with cockroaches and parasites, just for expressing their opinions and criticising the system?" Dipke told Agence France-Presse (AFP).

Dipke then went online in May to air his frustrations, making a satirical post on X that said: "What if all cockroaches come together?"

But the post went viral, driving Dipke to transform the idea into a parody platform that he named the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), playing on the name of the country's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

"Within two hours we got some 5,000 sign-ups on the Google form ... and that made me realise — why not launch an official website and a manifesto?" Dipke said.

More than 30,000 people joined within 24 hours of its launch. It now has more than 23 million followers on its Instagram account, eclipsing the BJP's by 14 million followers.

"That is when I realised maybe the youth here is trying to send a message," he said.

Dipke said momentum for the movement has been largely driven by gen Z students in their 20s.

"They told me they are really dissatisfied with all the existing political parties, because nobody listens to them," he said.

title.en: 'Anti-ICE' army veteran started fire outside Manhattan federal building, say officials
title.zh: 官员称，“反ICE”退伍军人在曼哈顿联邦大楼外开火

summary.en: Andrew Arrabaca, 43, was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks, says the FBI.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A former US Army soldier has been arrested after igniting a fire in front of a federal building in New York City, says the FBI.

Andrew Arrabaca, 43, allegedly shot a pellet gun and set off fireworks on Monday morning at 26 Federal Plaza, where the FBI, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and US Citizenship and Immigration Services have offices.

Federal agents tackled the suspect, who they say was armed with a machete and other weapons.

Three people sustained minor injuries in the incident, including an immigrant who was attending a status hearing, said the FBI. The lower Manhattan site has become a flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration policies.

The suspect, whom the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) called an "anti-ICE rioter", launched fireworks before pouring an accelerant on the stairs of an entrance to the building, causing a fire. The BBC has contacted DHS for comment.

Arrabaca "made several anti-government and anti-ICE statements during the incident", the FBI said.

FBI New York Assistant Director James Barnacle said during a news conference that Arrabaca was armed with two axes, a machete, three knives and fireworks.

He fired about five to seven pellets from an airsoft gun in the direction of the building, Barnacle said.

DHS said a bystander was grazed, and a security officer who tackled and detained Arrabaca sustained minor injuries.

Arrabaca, of Poughkeepsie, New York state, served in the regular Army from 2001-04 and in the Army National Guard-New York from 2004-05, according to the BBC's US partner CBS.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the incident "deeply disturbing" in a post on X.

"Our administration will continue to ensure that every New Yorker is safe in their city - and hold accountable any who threaten that," he said.
body.zh: 美国联邦调查局称，一名前美国陆军士兵在纽约市一座联邦大楼前纵火后被捕。 43 岁的安德鲁·阿拉巴卡 (Andrew Arrabaca) 据称于周一早上在联邦调查局 (FBI)、移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 以及美国公民及移民服务局 (ICE) 和美国公民及移民服务局 (ICE) 的办公地点联邦广场 26 号举行枪击事件并燃放烟花。 联邦特工逮捕了嫌疑人，称嫌疑人携带砍刀和其他武器。 联邦调查局称，三人在事件中受轻伤，其中包括一名正在参加身份听证会的移民。曼哈顿下城已成为抗议唐纳德·特朗普总统移民政策的热点。 这名嫌疑人被国土安全部 (DHS) 称为“反 ICE 暴徒”，他先燃放烟花，然后将助燃剂倒在大楼入口的楼梯上，引发火灾。 BBC 已联系国土安全部征求意见。 联邦调查局表示，阿拉巴卡“在事件中发表了数项反政府和反 ICE 的言论”。 联邦调查局纽约助理局长詹姆斯·巴纳克尔在新闻发布会上表示，阿拉巴卡携带两把斧子、一把砍刀、三把刀和烟花。 巴纳克尔说，他用气枪向建筑物方向发射了大约五到七颗子弹。 国土安全部表示，一名旁观者被擦伤，一名拦截并拘留阿拉巴卡的安全人员受轻伤。 据英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司报道，阿拉巴卡来自纽约州波基普西，2001-04 年在正规军服役，2004-05 年在纽约陆军国民警卫队服役。 纽约市市长 Zohran Mamdani 在 X 上发帖称这一事件“令人深感不安”。 他说：“我们的政府将继续确保每个纽约人在自己城市的安全，并追究任何威胁这一安全的人的责任。”

title.en: At least 27 dead and 83 missing after passenger ferry capsizes off Guyana
title.zh: 圭亚那客运渡轮倾覆，至少27人死亡，83人失踪

summary.en: An investigation has been launched after a passenger ferry capsized off Guyana, leaving at least 27 people dead and 83 missing. The prime minister expressed hope that more survivors would be found.
summary.zh: 圭亚那附近一艘客运渡轮倾覆，造成至少27人死亡，83人失踪，目前已展开调查。该国总理表示，希望有更多幸存者被找到。

body.en:
At least 27 people have drowned after a passenger ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana on Saturday night local time.

Sixty-nine people aboard the MV Barima had been rescued, Prime Minister Mark Phillips told reporters on Monday, adding 83 more remained missing.

Divers continue to search the site where the vessel capsized and people who believe their loved ones may have been on board the stricken vessel have been asked to contact the authorities.

"Let me be absolutely clear: where negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing is established, those responsible will face the full force of the law," he said.

Guyana's Public Works Minister, Juan Edghill, expressed his anger at a news conference on Sunday, accusing those who operated the ferry of trying to "cheat the system".

The official registry had listed 133 as being on board the ferry, but Phillips said on Monday he was now "confident" there were 179 people.

Edghill also said the ferry's captain and at least one crew member had tested positive for cannabis.

"We have zero tolerance for members of the crew drinking or smoking while at work. And for us to have positive tests from the captain... this is serious," the minister said.

He added the captain and several of his crew had been taken into police custody.

The ferry, MV Barima, departed from the capital, Georgetown, on Saturday afternoon local time, headed for Port Kaituma, in the north of the country.

The 40m-long (131ft) vessel was built in 1939, according to a listing on VesselFinder.

A survivor, Elena Moonsammy, told local news site Kiskadee Watch , external that the ferry had tilted after being hit by a large wave, with water quickly rushing in.

A distress call was received at 23:01 (03:01 GMT Sunday), triggering a search operation involving government teams and privately owned boats.

Moonsammy said she had survived by clinging to a box floating amidst the debris.

She had tried to hold on to the hand of her two-year-old child but they had been separated.

Moonsammy said she had managed to save a woman, whom she urged to also hold on to the floating box.

At least 15 children were among those rescued. Small private boats were key in pulling at least 17 survivors from the sea.

The French army sent 12 divers, two doctors and a mechanic from nearby French Guiana to aid the search-and-rescue operation.

Guyana's Health Minister, Dr Frank Anthony, said three of the survivors remained in hospital with minor injuries but the others had already been discharged.

title.en: Netanyahu may visit New York. Mamdani and Trump disagree on what awaits him

summary.en: Israel has dismissed an international court's arrest warrant for its prime minister as 'bogus', amidst reports of a potential visit to New York and differing opinions from commentators on the implications.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has reassured Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that he will not face arrest in the US, after New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was considering options for such a move.

The International Criminal Court (ICC) issued arrest warrants for Netanyahu in 2024, accusing him of using starvation as a method of warfare and intentionally directing attacks against civilians in Gaza. Israel has denied allegations of war crimes.

Mamdani told the New York Times newspaper that his city's legal department was actively considering legal options for Netanyahu's arrest, should the Israeli leader come to New York for the UN General Assembly in September.

"I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague. He's a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court," he said.

"I've also said that I will follow the laws that we have here in New York City because I believe that there is an importance in following the law as a leader who presides over our city."

He said he would use existing laws, not create new ones, to potentially enforce the ICC warrant.

"Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that's what we will do, but we won't be writing our own laws to that end."

On Tuesday, Trump said the Israeli prime minister would not be arrested in the US, while not addressing Mamdani's comments directly.

"Benjamin Netanyahu will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America," he said in a post on his Truth Social platform, adding that Netanyahu was assisting in the US' war against Iran.

"The only ones that should be arrested are the people that led Iran into this unprecedented SPIRAL OF DEATH AND DESTRUCTION."

Netanyahu's office earlier responded to Mamdani's comments, describing the warrant as "bogus" and the actions of the ICC prosecutor Karim Khan as "criminal". Khan is facing sexual misconduct allegations that he denies .

"The ICC is a kangaroo court that has no jurisdiction over Americans or Israelis," the office posted.

"Mamdani appears interested in diverting public attention from his follies and attacking the leader of the Jewish state and the only democracy in the Middle East."

Mamdani also came under attack by fellow US politicians, including Democrat senator for Pennsylvania John Fetterman, who said the mayor had "no way" to arrest Netanyahu, and echoed the Israeli leader's assertion that the US was not part of the court.

title.en: 'Kings of the World': Spain's World Cup stars get a hero's welcome from fans and royals
title.zh: “世界之王”：西班牙世界杯球星受到球迷和王室的英雄式欢迎

summary.en: Spain's World Cup-winning football team received a hero's welcome from the country's royals and celebrated with a bus parade through Madrid.

body.en:
New World Cup champions Spain enjoyed a vibrant celebration parade on an open-top bus through the streets of Madrid on Monday evening, with a jubilant crowd of an estimated two million people out to celebrate, according to local authorities.

The players, some shirtless, others holding drinks, set off on their procession under a blazing sun, along the main arteries in the city centre where a sea of fans in red and yellow were waiting, before arriving at Cibeles square where they took to the stage and partied into the night.

The squad and coach Luis de la Fuente were introduced one by one to the fans, each with their own choice of music that they sung along to, wearing "We are champions" shirts.

"(Spain) showed the world what it is to work together, with one mind and one heart," said pop superstar Shakira in a video message played to the team and crowd.

De la Fuente offered a similar message, hailing his players as the "best in the world" and telling fans not to forget that "together we are stronger".

After flying back from the United States to Madrid, the players were received by King Felipe VI and the royal family earlier Monday, and then Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez Pérez-Castejón, before kicking off the parade.

Players passed around the gleaming World Cup trophy and waved to their adoring supporters, some lining balconies, others on top of bus stops, the day after defeating Argentina 1-0 in extra-time in New Jersey.

Ferran Torres's strike in extra-time was enough to bring Spain their second World Cup, following a first victory in 2010.

"You have shown your grit, your resilience and your courage ... combining head and heart," the king told La Roja's stars, who were dressed in suits but changed to more casual clothing for their parade on a hot summer's day.

"Kings of the world" ran the words on the front of their vehicle, with fans chanting "champions" to their heroes.

Spain captain Rodri held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs as he descended from the Iberia plane that flew the team home after clinching their second star.

Later at Moncloa, Manchester City midfielder Rodri said this was the crowning achievement of his career.

"I've always said it, winning with your country is the most beautiful thing there is, above all a World Cup," said Rodri.

"This generation grew up watching (Iker) Casillas and (Andres) Iniesta lift the cup and that we can do it today is the biggest thing you can do in football."

Many younger supporters were not yet born when Iniesta's extra-time goal against the Netherlands secured Spain's first World Cup in South Africa 16 years ago.

title.en: Yemen's Houthis declare Saudi maritime blockade, threatening new front in US-Iran war
title.zh: 也门胡塞武装宣布对沙特进行海上封锁，威胁开辟美伊战争新战线

summary.en: Yemen's Houthi group has declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, threatening to open a new front in the ongoing conflict, to which the Saudi-led coalition has vowed a forceful response.
summary.zh: 也门胡塞武装宣布对沙特进行海上封锁，威胁在持续的冲突中开辟新战线，沙特领导的联军则誓言将“以武力”回应胡塞武装的威胁。

body.en:
Yemen's Houthi rebels announced a maritime embargo of Saudi Arabia overnight, stepping up the US-Iran war as the rebels threatened the top oil exporter's ability to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The Iran-backed group did not say how it planned to impose the embargo, whose declaration came as Iran said it was back to a "full-scale war" with the United States, and as Washington and Tehran battled to control the strait .

Saudi Arabia and the Houthis traded fire last week for the first time in years, threatening a 2022 truce that has held despite expiring .

The exchange of strikes was set off when an Iranian plane attempted to land in Sanaa, challenging Saudi Arabia's hegemony over Yemeni skies.

The Houthis' naval blockade, if enforced, could further strain Saudi Arabia's economy by cutting off access to its Red Sea ports, which have been vital for oil exports as renewed fighting limits passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

The blockade is also expected to hurt global markets that rely on Saudi Arabia — which produces over 10 million barrels of crude per day — for energy imports.

The rebels declared "a maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of 'an eye for an eye', effective immediately", military spokesman Yahya Saree said.

Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for the UN secretary-general, warned that the threat from the Houthis risked an "even wider" regional conflict.

The Houthis have previously tried to cut off shipping through the Red Sea, leveraging the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint at its southern tip which vessels must navigate when travelling to or from the Suez Canal and the Mediterranean.

Security expert Andreas Krieg said Tehran could ask the Houthis to "prepare the Bab al-Mandab front and may provide the strategic trigger, particularly if US pressure is degrading Iran's position around Hormuz" even if the rebels retain "considerable autonomy".

The full closure of the Bab al-Mandab strait would reduce global oil supply by 7 per cent as it would leave most of Saudi oil exports unable to leave the region. The disruption would add to the huge cut to oil flows from the US-Iran war, which has already reduced shipments by 10 per cent of global supply.

"A simultaneous crisis at Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab would produce a much larger shock than either blockade alone," the King's College London academic told Agence France-Presse.

title.en: Mexican drug lord ‘El Mayo’ sentenced to life without parole in US prison
title.zh: 墨西哥毒枭“埃尔·马约”在美国监狱被判无期徒刑

summary.en: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a co-founder of the notorious Sinaloa cartel and one of the world's most wanted drug traffickers, has been sentenced to life without parole in a US prison.
summary.zh: 臭名昭著的锡那罗亚贩毒集团联合创始人、全球头号毒枭之一伊斯梅尔·“埃尔·马约”·赞巴达，在美国被判处无期徒刑，不得假释。

body.en:
Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a co-founder of the Sinaloa cartel and one of the world's most notorious drug traffickers, was sentenced to life in a US prison.

Mexican drug trafficker Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole on Tuesday for co-founding and leading the notorious Sinaloa cartel .

Zambada was one of the most prominent Mexican drug traffickers to face sentencing in a United States court since Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman was sentenced to life in prison in 2019.

"The almost unimaginable amount of drugs attributable to him and the number of murders that we can document is enough to justify Congress's decision to make this a mandatory life sentence," US District Judge Brian Cogan said.

The 76-year-old Zambada apologized "for the harm I caused and for the example I set," urging future generations to "choose a different path."

He was arrested in July 2024 after he said he was kidnapped in Mexico and flown to Texas .

Zambada helped found and lead the Sinaloa cartel, becoming one of the most wanted figures for US intelligence and law enforcement agencies for decades.

According to prosecutors, he ordered torture and plotted murders, including the killing of his own nephew, as the cartel flooded the US with tons of cocaine, fentanyl, methamphetamine and other drugs .

He pleaded guilty to charges that included engaging in a continuing criminal enterprise and racketeering conspiracy, acknowledging culpability for 85 underlying crimes. In exchange, prosecutors did not seek the death penalty.

"I grew up in an environment where violence and crime seemed normal, but now I know that's no excuse," Zambada said in court on Monday. "There comes a time when every person must take responsibility for their decisions. I didn't, and many people paid the price."

Zambada's former partner "El Chapo" is already serving a life sentence in the United States.

He was convicted in 2019 and is serving a life sentence at the federal Supermax prison in Florence, Colorado.

Together they built the Sinaloa cartel into one of the world's most powerful drug trafficking organizations.

The Sinaloa cartel is one of six Mexican drug gangs that US President Donald Trump has designated as Foreign Terrorist Organizations.

Zambada was arrested with El Chapo's son, Joaquin Guzman Lopez , one of El Chapo's sons, who has pleaded guilty to federal drug charges. He has yet to be sentenced.

Zambada's arrest led to a splintering of the Sinaloa cartel, pitting his loyalists against backers of Guzman's sons, dubbed the Chapitos, or "little Chapos."

body.zh: 伊斯梅尔·“埃尔·梅奥”·赞巴达是锡那罗亚贩毒集团的联合创始人，也是世界上最臭名昭著的毒贩之一，在美国监狱被判处终身监禁。 周二，墨西哥毒贩伊斯梅尔·“埃尔·梅奥”·赞巴达因共同创立和领导臭名昭著的锡那罗亚贩毒集团而被判处终身监禁，不得假释。 自 2019 年“矮子”华金·古兹曼被判处终身监禁以来，赞巴达是在美国法院面临判刑的最著名的墨西哥毒贩之一。 美国地区法官布莱恩·科根 (Brian Cogan) 表示：“他所携带的几乎难以想象的毒品数量以及我们可以记录的谋杀案数量足以证明国会决定将其判处强制性无期徒刑。” 76岁的赞巴达“为我造成的伤害和我树立的榜样”道歉，并敦促后代“选择一条不同的道路”。 他于 2024 年 7 月被捕，此前他声称自己在墨西哥被绑架并飞往德克萨斯州。 赞巴达帮助创建并领导了锡那罗亚贩毒集团，成为美国情报和执法机构几十年来最想要的人物之一。 据检察官称，当该贩毒集团向美国大量运送可卡因、芬太尼、冰毒和其他毒品时，他下令实施酷刑并策划谋杀，包括杀害自己的侄子。 他对包括参与持续犯罪活动和共谋敲诈勒索在内的指控表示认罪，承认对 85 项基本犯罪负有责任。作为交换，检察官没有寻求死刑。 赞巴达周一在法庭上表示：“在我成长的环境中，暴力和犯罪似乎很常见，但现在我知道这不是借口。” “总有一天，每个人都必须为自己的决定负责。我没有，很多人为此付出了代价。” 赞巴达的前搭档“矮子”已经在美国服无期徒刑。 他于 2019 年被定罪，目前正在科罗拉多州佛罗伦萨的联邦 Supermax 监狱服无期徒刑。 他们共同将锡那罗亚贩毒集团打造成为世界上最强大的贩毒组织之一。 锡那罗亚贩毒集团是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普指定为外国恐怖组织的六个墨西哥贩毒团伙之一。 赞巴达与矮子的儿子华金·古兹曼·洛佩兹 (Joaquin Guzman Lopez) 一起被捕，华金·古兹曼·洛佩兹 (Joaquin Guzman Lopez) 已承认联邦毒品指控。他尚未被判刑。 赞巴达的被捕导致锡那罗亚贩毒集团的分裂，他的忠诚者与古兹曼儿子的支持者（被称为查皮托斯或“小矮子”）对立起来。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您依赖我们团队提供值得信赖的报告，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您将始终看到我们经过验证的...

title.en: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
title.zh: 速卖通（AliExpress）被欧盟处以创纪录罚款

summary.en: The Chinese retailer AliExpress has received a substantial fine from the European Union, becoming the latest online marketplace to be penalized under the EU’s Digital Services Act.
summary.zh: 中国零售商速卖通（AliExpress）被欧盟处以巨额罚款，成为最新一家因违反欧盟《数字服务法案》而受到处罚的在线市场。

body.en:
The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

AliExpress said it plans to appeal a penalty imposed by European Union (EU) regulators, who found shortcomings in the firm's efforts to curb illegal, unsafe and counterfeit goods.

The largest Chinese e-commerce platform in the EU, AliExpress, has been fined  €550 million ($629 million) for failing to tackle sales of illegal, unsafe and counterfeit products.

"The spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys, dangerous cosmetics and other illegal and harmful products is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online - it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations under the Digital Services Act," European Commission Vice President Henna Virkkunen said on Monday.

It is the largest fine ever imposed under the Digital Services Act (DSA) , which sets out clear rules for online services in the EU, targeting especially very large online platforms.

AliExpress said it will appeal the "disproportionate" fine, saying it considers the penalty excessive.

The online retail giant, which belongs to the Alibaba Group, must pay the fine and has until October 20, to submit a plan to address the breaches. EU regulators will then review the plan, after which the company could face further penalties.

A year ago, AliExpress agreed to tighten controls on illegal and potentially dangerous goods, such as medicines and supplements. But the European Commission said the measures did not fully resolve its broader concerns.

But AliExpress said the EU's decision "ignores our sound risk management framework and the significant, proactive enhancements we have made."

The company also said it has worked with the Commission to meet its "evolving expectations."

According to the EU, AliExpress has 193 million users in the bloc, ahead of online fashion giant Shein and retailer Temu, which have 156 million and 130 million users, respectively.

"One in five Europeans say they shop once a month from Shein, Temu and AliExpress," Virkkunen said.

Temu was fined  €200 million in May , while Elon Musk's social media platform X was fined in December last year, both for DSA violations.

title.en: Russia says bus strike kills 5 in border region with Ukraine
title.zh: 俄罗斯称乌克兰边境地区公交车袭击致5人死亡

summary.en: Russia reported that a bus strike killed five people in a border region with Ukraine, following Ukraine's launch of hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯报告称，在乌克兰向莫斯科发射数百架无人机，以回应俄罗斯对基辅的导弹袭击后，一次公交车袭击造成与乌克兰接壤的边境地区五人死亡。

body.en:
The strike comes as Ukraine launched more than hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv, as President Zelenskyy sought to calm growing tensions over Ukraine’s military leadership.

Russia said Monday that a Ukrainian strike on a bus in the border region of Belgorod killed five civilians, including a minor, and left three others critically injured.

The attack came after a Ukrainian retaliatory strike on Moscow, with city officials reporting that more than 400 drones targeted the Russian capital.

The latest escalation followed Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities over the weekend.

In eastern Ukraine , Russian attacks on Pavlograd and Kramatorsk killed two people in each city, according to local authorities.

Officials also reported one person killed in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia during Russian bombardment.

Ukraine targeted the Russian capital with more than 400 drones from Sunday into Monday, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

He added that most of the drones were intercepted, but Moscow region Gov. Andrei Vorobyov said at least 10 people were wounded by Ukrainian drones.

Several residential buildings and civilian infrastructure facilities were also damaged.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces were targeting Russian logistics facilities and an oil depot in the region.

"We are responding, justly, to every Russian strike against our cities and communities," Zelenskyy said in a post on X.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's military publicly denied rumors that Zelenskyy was firing the chief of Ukraine's armed forces, Oleksandr Syrskyi.

Zelenskyy has faced criticism over the dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov last week.

There have been days of protests in Ukraine following Fedorov's removal, as a long-running dispute between the reform-minded minister and Syrskyi spilled into the open.

Zelenskyy appointed Yevhenii Khmara, the acting head of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), as acting defense minister and asked parliament to approve him for the position.

On Monday, he posted several messages on social media showing him meeting with Ukraine's top military commanders to discuss the latest developments in the war, which has dragged on for more than four years.

title.en: Guterres to visit Cyprus as UN seeks to revive peace talks
title.zh: 古特雷斯将访问塞浦路斯，联合国寻求恢复和谈

summary.en: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is scheduled to visit Cyprus next week to try and restart the stalled peace process. The visit aims to explore new avenues for dialogue and potential solutions to the long-standing conflict.
summary.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯定于下周访问塞浦路斯，旨在重启陷入僵局的和平进程。此次访问旨在探索新的对话途径和解决长期冲突的潜在方案。

body.en:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will visit Cyprus next week in what is seen as an effort to kickstart the stalled peace process. Why now? What is known about the plan? And what might be different this time round?

Monday marks the 52nd anniversary of Turkey's 1974 invasion of Cyprus , which led to the division of the island.

Five decades later, the Cyprus issue remains one of the world's longest-running unresolved disputes.

The United Nations announced last week that Antonio Guterres  was due to visit Cyprus from July 27 to 29 — the first visit by a UN secretary-general in 16 years — in an effort to breathe new life into the stalled peace process.

His visit marks the culmination of a renewed UN initiative that was launched after an informal enlarged meeting on Cyprus held in Geneva in March.

Since then, the UN secretary-general's personal envoy, Maria Angela Holguin, has held a series of consultations in Cyprus, Greece, Turkey , the United Kingdom and Brussels to assess whether the political conditions exist for meaningful negotiations to resume.

During his stay in Cyprus, Guterres will hold separate meetings with  President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman.

On July 29, the two leaders are expected to meet jointly with the UN chief at the residence of the UN Special Representative in the UN-controlled buffer zone.

The last time a UN secretary-general visited Cyprus was in 2010, when Ban Ki-moon sought to inject political momentum into negotiations between then President of the Republic of Cyprus Demetris Christofias and Turkish Cypriot leader Mehmet Ali Talat.

Both leaders came from left-wing political parties that supported a bizonal, bicommunal federation and were widely seen as having the political will to pursue a comprehensive settlement.

That momentum, however, faded only months later after Talat lost the Turkish Cypriot leadership election to Dervis Eroglu, while major disagreements over the core chapters of the negotiations remained unresolved.

Ban's efforts were preceded by the intensive engagement of Kofi Annan between 2002 and 2004, when the UN undertook its most ambitious effort to broker a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus issue.

Annan became personally involved in the negotiations, presenting a series of revised versions of what became known as the Annan Plan.

The initiative culminated in simultaneous referendums in April 2004. The proposal was approved by a majority of Turkish Cypriot voters but rejected by 75.8% of Greek Cypriot voters.

The announcement of Guterres' visit comes amid reports that the UN is exploring a possible new framework for resolving the Cyprus issue.

body.zh: 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯将于下周访问塞浦路斯，此举被视为旨在启动陷入僵局的和平进程。为什么是现在？关于该计划有哪些已知信息？这次可能会有什么不同？ 周一是土耳其 1974 年入侵塞浦路斯 52 周年，这次入侵导致了塞浦路斯岛的分裂。 五年后，塞浦路斯问题仍然是世界上持续时间最长的未解决争端之一。 联合国上周宣布，安东尼奥·古特雷斯将于 7 月 27 日至 29 日访问塞浦路斯，这是联合国秘书长 16 年来的首次访问，旨在为陷入僵局的和平进程注入新的活力。 他的访问标志着联合国新倡议的高潮，该倡议是三月份在日内瓦举行的塞浦路斯问题非正式扩大会议后发起的。 此后，联合国秘书长个人特使玛丽亚·安吉拉·奥尔金在塞浦路斯、希腊、土耳其、英国和布鲁塞尔举行了一系列磋商，以评估是否存在恢复有意义的谈判的政治条件。 在塞浦路斯逗留期间，古特雷斯将分别与塞浦路斯共和国总统尼科斯·赫里斯托杜利德斯和土族塞人领导人图凡·埃尔胡曼举行会晤。 7月29日，两国领导人预计将在位于联合国控制缓冲区的联合国特别代表官邸与联合国秘书长共同会晤。 联合国秘书长上次访问塞浦路斯是在 2010 年，当时潘基文试图为时任塞浦路斯共和国总统德米特里斯·赫里斯托菲亚斯和土族塞人领导人穆罕默德·阿里·塔拉特之间的谈判注入政治动力。 两位领导人都来自支持两区两族联邦的左翼政党，并被广泛认为具有寻求全面解决方案的政治意愿。 然而，几个月后，塔拉特在土族塞人领导人选举中输给德尔维斯·埃罗格鲁后，这种势头就消退了，而谈判核心章节的重大分歧仍未解决。 在潘基文做出努力之前，科菲·安南在 2002 年至 2004 年期间大力参与，当时联合国为促成塞浦路斯问题的全面解决做出了最雄心勃勃的努力。 安南亲自参与了谈判，提出了一系列被称为“安南计划”的修订版本。 该倡议最终于 2004 年 4 月同时举行全民公投。该提案获得大多数土族塞人选民的批准，但遭到 75.8% 希族塞人选民的拒绝。 古特雷斯宣布访问之际，有报道称联合国正在探索解决塞浦路斯问题的可能新框架。 英国《独立报》发表后，讨论愈演愈烈……

Even when dialogue stalls, the work of peacemaking remains vital, reflecting a deep desire for harmony in a fractured world. title.en: China, Philippines clash in South China Sea ahead of ASEAN meeting

summary.en: China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.

Sailors from the Chinese and Philippine navies faced off with oars and batons in the disputed South China Sea , with Philippine officials saying that one of its sailors suffered a head injury as a result of the altercation.

The latest confrontation took place on Monday near the Second Thomas Shoal, a contested area where the two countries have repeatedly clashed before .  The  Philippines keeps a military presence in the area aboard the grounded warship BRP Sierra Madre.

Manila said that Chinese Coast Guard personnel had assaulted Filipino sailors as they approached the outpost. 

China quickly rejected this narrative. Beijing's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that the "Philippine side provoked the incident first," by approaching the Chinese vessel in small rubber boats, but then "turned around ​and made counter-accusations, distorted the facts and engaged in malicious ​hype."

On Tuesday, China summoned the Philippine ambassador in Beijing to lodge its complaints, with the Philippines quickly following suit with the Chinese counterpart in Manila.

The Second Thomas Shoal is part of the Spratly islands, a disputed archipelago in the South China Sea.

The Spratlys are key to Beijing's claim of the entire South China Sea, a key global trade route. Beijing maintains its claim to the waterway despite a 2016 ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague that there is no legal basis to its argument.

China has repeatedly demanded the removal of the outpost on the BRP Sierra Madre, and surrounded the atoll with its ships in a tense territorial standoff that has dragged on for years.

The incident came just ahead of a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) which was set to begin on Tuesday with foreign ministers of the eleven member states and external partners.

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong, who was in Manila for the summit, denounced Beijing on Tuesday for what she called "destabilizing and dangerous conduct" during the standoff.

Wong, during a visit to the headquarters of the Philippine Coast Guard, also announced a support package for the agency totaling 10 million Australian dollars ($6.7 million) for drone technology.

The US State Department also issued a statement criticizing China's actions, saying its "troubling pattern of provocations against the Philippines' legitimate maritime operations undermines regional peace and stability."

body.en: Startling new research shows that in many countries – including old US allies – the public prefers Beijing to Washington Earlier this year, a spate of western TikTok and Instagram creators announced that they were at “a very Chinese time in my life” – drinking hot water and wearing slippers around their homes. The Chinamaxxing phenomenon primarily reflected the constant need of influencers for novel content. But social media trends also reflect a growing fascination with China, as the economic historian Adam Tooze has noted . While it broods over China’s economic, military and technical advance, the Trump administration is accelerating Beijing’s diplomatic progress, as striking new polling by the Pew Research Center shows. For the first time, China and Xi Jinping are seen more favourably than the US and its president in most of the 36 major countries surveyed – including Canada, Mexico and Australia. Only in six countries did people rate the US more highly. While Beijing has seen significant improvements in some places, the slump in Washington’s standing is more dramatic. Across 20 countries, the median percentage with a favourable view of China rose from 32% to 46% between 2023 and this year; for the US, it fell from 58% to 36%. Views of China were much more positive in Latin America, Africa and parts of south and south-east Asia than in wealthier European and east Asian countries. Continue reading...
body.zh: 令人震惊的新研究表明，在许多国家 — — 包括美国的老盟友 — — 公众更喜欢北京而不是华盛顿。 今年早些时候，一大批西方 TikTok 和 Instagram 创作者宣布，他们正处于“我一生中非常中国化的时期”——喝着热水，在家中穿着拖鞋。 Chinamaxshing现象主要反映了网红对新颖内容的持续需求。但正如经济历史学家亚当·图兹（Adam Tooze）指出的那样，社交媒体趋势也反映出人们对中国日益增长的迷恋。皮尤研究中心令人震惊的最新民意调查显示，在关注中国经济、军事和技术进步的同时，特朗普政府正在加速北京的外交进展。在接受调查的 36 个主要国家（包括加拿大、墨西哥和澳大利亚）中，大多数国家对中国和习近平的好感度首次高于美国及其总统。只有六个国家的人们对美国的评价更高。尽管北京在某些方面取得了显着进步，但华盛顿的地位下滑更为严重。 2023 年至今，20 个国家对中国持好感的中位数百分比从 32% 上升至 46%；美国则从 58% 下降至 36%。拉丁美洲、非洲以及南亚和东南亚部分地区对中国的看法比富裕的欧洲和东亚国家要积极得多。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The shifting global perceptions of superpowers, as highlighted in the news, remind us that a nation's true standing is often tied to its character and actions. Proverbs 14:34 suggests that righteousness elevates a people, while moral failings can bring disgrace. This perspective encourages us to consider how nations, like individuals, are ultimately judged...

verse.textEn: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin condemns any people.
verse.textZh: 公义使邦国高举；罪恶是人民的羞辱。

title.en: China firm seeks damages over state control of British Steel

summary.en: China's Jingye Group is seeking compensation from the UK government after the government took over British Steel last year. The UK government intervened to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility, which Jingye Group had purchased in 2020.
summary.zh: 中国敬业集团正向英国政府寻求赔偿，此前英国政府去年接管了英国钢铁公司，以防止该国最后一个主要炼钢设施关闭。敬业集团于2020年收购了该公司。

body.en:
The UK government took over British Steel last year to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility. China's Jingye Group, which bought the firm in 2020, claims it is owed compensation.

A Chinese steel giant demanded compensation from the United Kingdom   government on Sunday, claiming the state's takeover of its subsidiary, British Steel, was "outright robbery."

The UK government took operational control of British Steel last year, after owner Jingye Group warned that Britain's last factory capable of making steel from scratch was no longer financially viable.

In a statement on social media, Jingye threatened legal action against the UK government, accusing ministers of "trampling on international investment rules."

Describing the nationalization as "outright robbery," the Chinese firm said it "reserves all legal rights, firmly defends its lawful rights and interests, and will pursue full compensation through legal means to the very end."

"The UK disregarded Jingye's continuous investment and significant contribution and was only willing to provide almost zero compensation,” the statement continued.

The company noted that nationalization could cost UK taxpayers more than 1.5 billion pounds ($2.02 billion, €1.76 billion) by 2028.

Jingye said it had begun a procedure under bilateral investment agreements to seek damages, without expanding further.

China's Foreign Ministry backed the compensation move, calling on the UK to "earnestly respect market principles and the spirit of contract, and find solutions on compensation and other issues acceptable to both sides."

After Jingye last year planned to close the blast furnaces at its plant in Scunthorpe, in northern England, the UK government passed emergency measures, allowing it to take  operational control of British Steel .

The immediate concern was that the blast furnaces would be shut permanently, ending the UK's capacity to produce virgin or primary steel from raw materials. The plant accounts for the vast majority of British Steel's operations.

The government cited national security for the move, which came five years after Jingye bought British Steel from a London-based private equity firm for around 70 million pounds.

Ministers cited the need to protect strategic steel supplies for construction, rail infrastructure and defense.

The move was also seen as a way to protect thousands of jobs in a deprived area of the UK. The Scunthorpe plant currently employs about 2,700 people.

In recent weeks, the UK Parliament has passed legislation that allowed the government on Thursday to bring British Steel into full public ownership.

body.en: As the bombing starts again, it’s clear the president has dragged the US into a limitless fiasco – and the world into an economic quagmire Feckless and clueless, Donald Trump is lost in Iran, unable to find a way out of the disastrous war he started. title.en: 'Shocking vulnerabilities': Trump makes sweeping claims China meddled in US elections
title.zh: “令人震惊的漏洞”：特朗普就中国干预美国大选发表全面声明

summary.en: The US president made broad election security claims, laying groundwork for the federal government to take action.
summary.zh: 美国总统就选举安全问题发表了广泛声明，为联邦政府采取行动奠定了基础。

body.en:
In a speech attacking US election integrity on Friday, US President Donald Trump released intelligence that he said showed major Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his false claims he won the 2020 election.

Trump's allegations about the "shocking vulnerabilities" in the American electoral system appeared to lay the groundwork for the Republican to dispute the results of November's crucial US midterm elections .

It underscored Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm vote, when Republicans in Congress will face the prospect of losing control of both the House of Representatives and Senate — an outcome that would carry significant political consequences for Trump.

"We can never watch a stolen election again," Trump said in the primetime address, referencing his 2020 presidential election defeat by Democrat Joe Biden.

Trump said he was declassifying huge amounts of intelligence data that showed, among other things, that superpower rival China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Over a period of years, starting during the 2020 election cycle, the People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history," Trump said in the televised speech from the White House.

He asserted that members of the US intelligence community deliberately suppressed information about the extent of China's activities.

His allegations contradict an unclassified 2021 US intelligence community assessment that found no indications any foreign actor tried to alter or succeeded in altering "any technical aspect" of the 2020 presidential election vote.

The assessment was conducted under John Ratcliffe, then Trump's director of national intelligence and now his CIA director.

Trump also claimed there were more than 250,000 non-US citizens registered to vote in four states.

body.en:
Less than four per cent of the social homes promised by the Albanese government's signature social housing fund have been delivered, two years into a five-year target period.

As of May 2026, 1432 of the Housing Australia Future Fund's target of 40,000 new social and affordable homes had been delivered, the Australian National Audit Office found in a report released on Tuesday.

The $10 billion fund's forecast to hit its target by mid-2029 faced "considerable uncertainty" as of June, the auditor-general found.

It's another setback for the government's broader housing supply agenda, with the construction industry about a year behind on its target to deliver 1.2 million new homes in the five years to June 2029.

Meanwhile, the social housing waitlist has grown from 155,000 to 169,000 in the 10 years to June 2024.

While Treasury was largely effective in designing the fund, the department had failed to take clear responsibility for delivering the program and provided little transparency about how it was progressing, the audit found.

Although funding applications opened in January 2024, Treasury had not finalised delivery arrangements until May 2026.

"The delayed finalisation of most governance and oversight arrangements has limited the ability of Treasury to systematically monitor and manage program risks and performance over time," the auditor-general said.

"Once finalised, Treasury has not always implemented governance and oversight arrangements as intended, with sometimes out-of-date and inconsistent arrangements.

The fund works by giving money to providers to either build new homes or purchase newly constructed homes from developers.

Once built, homes are subsidised by the government to provide tenants below-market rates for 25 years, at a cost of about $393,000 per dwelling in today's money.

Of the 1432 homes delivered by the fund, 762 were new homes constructed by housing providers, and 670 were newly built by private developers and purchased by a housing provider before, during or immediately after development.

The audit made five recommendations to improve governance, risk management, performance review and transparency of the program.

Housing Minister Clare O'Neil welcomed the report findings and accepted all recommendations.

"Importantly, the report found Treasury's design of the Housing Australia Future Fund was largely effective and supported by largely sound policy advice," she said.

"This program is being delivered in one of the toughest construction markets in decades.

title.en: The secret spy base many Australians know almost nothing about
title.zh: 许多澳大利亚人几乎一无所知的秘密间谍基地

summary.en: In the heart of Australia, a top-secret facility has drawn intrigue and controversy for decades.

body.en:
It's been nearly 60 years since a mysterious spy base was opened in a sacred stretch of Australian outback. Even today, what happens inside Pine Gap remains a closely guarded secret.

There's been renewed focus on the joint United States-Australian intelligence facility this week after hundreds of protesters gathered there to protest its existence.

Located 18km south-west of Alice Springs, the top-secret base is often described as one of Australia’s most secure and secretive facilities.

Its most recognisable feature is the cluster of large white domes scattered across the site. The facility uses satellite equipment to collect intelligence and detect missile launches.

The three-day gathering over the weekend marked the 60th anniversary of the agreement between the US and Australia that paved the way for the construction of the facility on Arrernte Country.

In a statement to SBS News, the defence department said the government does not comment on intelligence matters or the operation of its joint facilities.

The facility has been a source of scrutiny and controversy since it was established by the US' Central Intelligence Agency in the late 1960s to gather intelligence on Soviet missile tests during the Cold War.

It's expanded in scale and capacity over the decades, and has drawn repeated protest action, including a major demonstration in 1987 that saw more than 1,000 protesters march up to its gates. Organisers said Monday's protest was the largest since then.

In 1983, hundreds of women camped outside Pine Gap as part of a two-week peace protest, arguing it made Australia a nuclear target and tied the country to the US military machine.

In Alice Springs, where Census data puts the population at around 26,000, it employs around 800 of the town's residents, ABC Backstory reported in 2024. According to that reporting, locals remain divided over the facility.

Some view it as vital to the local economy, while some still fear it makes Alice Springs a nuclear target.

The Australian Federal Police, in a recruitment page for protective service officers at Pine Gap, describes it as one of its "most unique and critical protection sites".

Anti-war and anti- AUKUS campaigners, as well as pro-Palestinian solidarity groups, participated in the gathering over the weekend, calling for greater scrutiny of the facility's role in the Hamas-Israel war.

Last year, United Nations investigators accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza during the war, an accusation which Israel denies.

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson says she's "totally opposed" to the war in Ukraine, but did not say whether she still believes that Russian President Vladimir Putin is a "strong man".

The right-wing leader was in Perth on Tuesday addressing a business breakfast after returning from Europe, where she faced scrutiny after holidaying in an Italian resort town with mining magnate Gina Rinehart, attending a luxury fashion show and speaking on a podcast with controversial far-right activist Tommy Robinson.

SBS News asked Hanson at a press conference on the sidelines of the business event whether she stood by her comments in 2017 praising Putin as a leader who had gained the respect of his country.

During the 2017 ABC Insiders interview, Hanson described Putin as a "patriotic" leader who was "doing so well for his country".

"Even people here in Australia were saying, 'I wish we had a leader like that here in Australia. I wish someone would stand up and fight for this country,'" she told the program.

She also questioned his involvement in the downing of flight MH17, asking: "Have you got the proof he did it? Did he push the button?"

When asked about the comments on Tuesday, Hanson said: "I don't like what Putin has done in the invasion of Ukraine. I'm totally opposed to that."

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with more than 16,000 Ukrainian civilians killed so far, according to the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, in a move against international law.

Putin has since been issued an arrest warrant by the world court for the 'unlawful deportation' of Ukrainian children in 2023. The Kremlin has rejected the accusation.

One Nation has been under separate scrutiny after comments, first reported by Nine newspapers, by its Queensland senator Malcolm Roberts on a 2025 podcast, in which he said: "When I look at the Ukraine war, I see Putin as standing up to the globalists and earning my respect for doing so. He knows what’s going on in Ukraine and it's a war against the globalists."

About three dozen uniformed and plain clothes police were deployed around and inside the Crown resort complex in Perth, where the One Nation leader was speaking.

About 200 protesters were out the front chanting "we say no to white Australia".

Hanson again denied advocating for the return of the White Australia policy after citing the discriminatory immigration scheme in an interview with Robinson during her European trip.

title.en: 'Unpredictable': New warning for Australians travelling abroad
title.zh: “不可预测”：澳大利亚政府对海外旅行发出新警告

summary.en: The Australian government has issued a new warning for citizens traveling abroad, citing escalating global conflicts that could lead to flight disruptions and changes to travel plans.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚政府对公民海外旅行发出新警告，指出全球冲突升级可能导致航班中断和旅行计划变更。

body.en:
The government is urging Australians to reconsider travel to Oman, Jordan and Saudi Arabia amid re-escalating conflict in the Middle East .

The latest advice on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's Smartraveller website said the situation in the Middle East "remains unpredictable" and there is "risk of more attacks and escalation".

"Military conflict in the Middle East has also caused widespread fuel supply shortages, flight cancellations and other travel disruptions worldwide," it said.

"Your travel plans may be affected, even if your destination is not in the Middle East."

The warning noted that military strikes and reprisal attacks have been carried out in a number of locations across the Middle East in recent days, including those directed at targets in each of the three countries.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Oman, Jordan and Saudi Arabia have been upgraded to level three, which advises Australians to reconsider their need to travel and avoid non-essential travel there.

Level three, according to the site's warning system, indicates serious and potentially life-threatening risks that can make a location unsafe for tourism and unsuitable for most travellers.

"We now advise 'reconsider your need to travel' overall due to the unpredictable security situation," Smartraveller said.

The three nations join Bahrain, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates at level three.

Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, the Palestinian territories, Syria and Yemen remain at the highest alert level, which advises Australians not to travel there at all.

For Australians already in the Middle East who want to leave, the government continues to advise them to do so while commercial flights are available if it's safe to travel to an airport.

body.en:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has sparked a new discussion about the resurgence of a 'White Australia' policy — a controversial series of laws that discriminated against non-European migrants.

Hanson, during an appearance on a podcast with the British far-right, anti-immigration activist and convicted criminal Tommy Robinson last week, suggested that scrapping the White Australia policy was the root cause of apparent migration issues in Australia.

"It started in 1973 with Gough Whitlam, so they opened up and got rid of the White Australia policy, then they started bringing in the different migrants," she said.

She's since insisted that she doesn't support the policy, but a new wave of anti-immigration sentiment has sparked questions about whether Australia risks reviving aspects of it.

White Australia wasn't a single policy, but a series of laws that limited non-British migration to Australia.

"It essentially believed that Australia needed to be a homogenous white culture," Benjamin T Jones, an Australian political history expert, told SBS News.

"It prioritised immigration, especially from white British settlers, who they believed would integrate best into an Australian society."

It began with the Immigration Restriction Act 1901, which included a dictation test of 50 words in any European language, which became the way certain people ended up being excluded from Australia.

"You were never intended to pass it. It's a test that was designed to be failed," Mark Cully, the author of a new book on Australia's immigration economic history, told SBS News.

Even after the test was removed, it remained difficult for those who weren't European or North American to obtain permits to Australia, Cully says, and they were effectively excluded from applying for permanent residence.

The end of the White Australia policy began under Harold Holt in the 1960s, and it was dismantled under the Whitlam government in 1975, when the Racial Discrimination Act was passed, making it illegal to "offend, insult, humiliate or intimidate" someone because of their race.

"It's kind of astonishing in some ways that that policy, which is so ingrained and normalised and seen by many Australians as uncontroversial for 60 odd years, was then unwound, roughly over a decade," Cully said.

"Since then, we've had the embrace of multiculturalism. Australia and Canada really stand out across the world as being exemplar countries for welcoming migrants from anywhere in the world and doing it in a fairly objective and considered and non-discriminatory way."

body.en:
Labour leader Andy Burnham has become the United Kingdom's seventh prime minister in a decade — but experts say it remains unclear how the former mayor of Greater Manchester will approach the country's most important strategic partnership with Australia.

Newly departed UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer suffered a high-profile split with his defence secretary, John Healey, over a perceived failure to properly fund the department.

Burnham now inherits Starmer's £298bn ($573b) defence spending commitment over the next four years, £4.7b ($9b) of which is unfunded and will need to make up part of Burnham's first budget.

Experts have said that, while Burnham is unlikely to renegotiate the AUKUS agreement, defence is likely to play a central position in the new UK leader's job description, given the growing threat of Russia to NATO members.

Jennifer Parker, a non-resident fellow at the Lowy Institute, told SBS News that policymakers in Australia will be watching Burnham's approach to foreign affairs closely.

"I think there are broader questions about the implications of Andy Burnham's views on defence and the defence investment plan in the UK ... [but] in many ways, AUKUS is critical for the UK," Parker told SBS News.

The UK, alongside Australia and the United States, entered into trilateral AUKUS security agreement in 2021.

The deal is divided into two key pillars: Australia's acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarine capability and the development and delivery of advanced capabilities such as underwater drones .

In July 2025, Australia also entered into a bilateral agreement with the UK dubbed the Geelong Treaty. The 50-year agreement enables the cooperative design, building, operation, sustainment, and disposal of nuclear-powered submarines known as SSN.

Since 1968, the UK has been a member of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and is recognised as one of the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council.

"Now, you need to have SSN's — attack submarines — to be able to protect your ballistic missile submarines. AUKUS, for the UK makes designing, building and operating SSN's cheaper. So, it makes it easier."

That's why she believes the UK, whether led by current UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer or the incoming Burnham, will continue to uphold its AUKUS commitments .

"If the UK can't achieve AUKUS ... the long-term impact is quite significant in terms of the UK ceases to be a nuclear weapons power. Which really changes its global status."

body.en:
Israel's embassy has rebuked the Labor party's draft national platform, warning its wording on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict places sole "responsibility" on the Jewish state while overlooking the role of Hamas and Palestinian leadership.

The four-page statement is a highly unusual intervention by a foreign government ahead of the party's national conference in Adelaide.

Labor's 2026 platform, which outlines the party's priorities and beliefs, contains an expanded statement on "Israel and Palestine" following the government's move to recognise Palestinian statehood , a longstanding part of the party platform.

The document reiterates support for a two-state solution, and also says the party "unreservedly condemns terrorism and violent extremism, including as perpetrated by Hamas and other extremists," stating Israelis and Palestinians deserve to live their lives free from terror and violence.

The platform says Israel "must comply with obligations as an occupying power" in supplying food and medical supplies for Palestinian civilians under international humanitarian law, and also condemns recent Knesset laws around the death penalty as "discriminatory."

The 'Death Penalty for Terrorists' law passed in March — and a subsequent 2026 military tribunal law — mandate capital punishment for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. The United Nations Human Rights Office warned the laws breach international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes.

The unsigned Israeli embassy statement, released on Monday, reads: "The Embassy respectfully submits that several elements of the draft National Platform risk placing responsibility for the conflict on one party while giving insufficient attention to the decisions, conduct and continuing obligations of the Palestinian leadership and terrorist organisations such as Hamas."

"Israel has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to make difficult compromises when genuine peace is possible."

While continuing to oppose Palestinian recognition, which the Australian government declared sovereign and independent in September 2025, Israel's embassy also disputed language in the draft platform condemning "extremist settler violence," which the government in June warned was at "horrific levels".

The embassy said settler violence "receives disproportionate attention," labelling it a "reprehensible but marginal phenomenon".

summary.en: Self-described misogynist Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were arrested over the weekend in the US and face charges in multiple jurisdictions.

body.en:
On Sunday, social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested in Miami in the United States, after authorities in the United Kingdom issued 38 new charges against the brothers, deepening the pair's international legal saga and adding further complication to an already fraught legal situation.

The United Kingdom's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has charged the brothers — who deny all wrongdoing — with fresh counts of rape, actual bodily harm, and human trafficking.

The new accusations add to a mountain of serious charges against the pair and could lead to the brothers' extradition from the US, assuming it is approved by the US state department.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate are dual US-UK citizens who have risen to prominence as social media influencers.

Andrew started his career in public life as a kickboxer and has gone on to become a prominent figure in the online 'manosphere' space, describing himself as a misogynist and encouraging his more than 10 million followers to follow in his footsteps.

He primarily posts on X, having been banned from YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines.

Stephanie Wescott, a lecturer in humanities and social science at Monash University, described Andrew as the "main character" of this content, while his brother Tristan is more of a "side figure".

She said the Tates have turned disrespecting and abusing women into a business model that glamorises male dominance, 'teaching' men how to emulate them through an online academy.

"[They promote] anti-feminism, anti-gender-equality, and hyper-masculinity or, you know, 'men being men' or men going back to a type of manhood that no longer exists," she said.

"One of their business models has been to train other young men into becoming the sort of influencers that they claim that they are.

"Part of that business model has also been to exploit and harm the girls and women around you and to use their images as currency to sell online — we know Australian men have signed up for these services.

The pair have also expressed support for US President Donald Trump, and Trump's eldest son, Donald Trump Jr, spoke out against the brothers' detention in Romania in 2023.

"The other layer to this is, of course, that they have this incredible political proximity to Donald Trump," Wescott said.

In 2025, Andrew Tate said he was "very close with the Trump family". Trump himself has said little about the Tates, however.

"They have been supported and aided by adjacent figures, podcasters such as Joe Rogan and others like him," Wescott continued.
